review_notes: Source-first scope: Table 5 equation (4) is the principal family testing whether the Big 6 auditor effect on DAC differs between income-increasing (Cp) and income-decreasing (Cg) incentive settings. The full sample is retained as the benchmark; Cp and Cg are co-primary directional populations needed for the central question. Eq. (2) DAC construction and annual Eq. (3) probit fits are required supporting regressions. Table 3 mean comparisons, the pooled Eq. (3) probit (not used to form retained Mills ratios), AWCA, alternate incentive proxies, and later sensitivity partitions are excluded.

Applied the sweep clarification distinguishing a substantive empirical question from development of an input measure: the paper asks a substantive audit-effectiveness question, and Eq. (2) is supporting because its residual is the retained DAC outcome. No scope revision was needed for the first two checkpointed substantive studies.

Table 5 reports aggregate observation totals across 15 annual fits; per-year second-stage N is unknown. The annual probit support is also repeated by year with no per-year N. The pooled first-stage probit is reported in Table 4, but does not generate the inverse Mills ratios used in Table 5 and is excluded.

Table 5 note refers to the auditor-choice model as equation (4), but equation (4) is the accrual-choice equation; the definitions and procedure identify the probit in equation (3) as the source of Lambda.

Equation (4) prose defines CFO as operating cash flows scaled by total assets, while the Table 5 row label specifies lagged total assets; the table-specific scaled measure is retained with the discrepancy flagged.

The pooled and annual Table 4 estimates are alternative presentations of equation (3); the retained annual probits are the ones actually used in the Table 5 selection correction. Equation (2) is estimated separately by two-digit SIC and year; Cp/Cg classification is at firm-year level, as endnote 18 clarifies.
